title: Temporal Photography Studio Simulator
description: The user operates an antique camera on a tripod to photograph a morphing test subject under various lighting and exposure conditions. Each photograph captures the interpolation state of the test model, and the user must balance energy conservation between flash intensity, ambient lighting, and exposure time while managing an undo/redo history of their studio adjustments.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 that implements a photography studio simulation. Load AntiqueCamera.glb centered-left on a draggable tripod mount and InterpolationTest.glb centered-right as the photographic subject. Add a ground plane with a subtle grid texture and a backdrop wall behind the subject.

Implement these coupled controls in a floating UI panel: (1) Flash Intensity slider 0-100%, (2) Ambient Light slider 0-100%, (3) Exposure Time slider 0.1-5.0 seconds, (4) Subject Animation Phase slider 0-1 controlling InterpolationTest morph/animation progress, (5) Camera Zoom via scroll wheel adjusting AntiqueCamera's focal framing. Enforce an energy conservation law: Flash + Ambient must always total exactly 100% — adjusting one auto-adjusts the other inversely.

The user can orbit the scene with left-click drag. Right-clicking the AntiqueCamera model triggers a 'capture' that freezes the current frame into a polaroid thumbnail in a filmstrip UI at the bottom (max 8 captures). Each polaroid stores all parameter states. Clicking a polaroid restores those exact settings. Implement full undo/redo with Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y that tracks every slider change, capture, and polaroid restoration as discrete history steps.

Add a shutter animation on the AntiqueCamera when capturing: brief flash overlay scaled by flash intensity, camera shake proportional to exposure time, and a film-advance sound placeholder via a visual indicator. The InterpolationTest model should play its embedded animations/morphs driven by the phase slider. Apply post-processing bloom scaled to flash intensity. Use a warm point light near the camera and a hemisphere light for ambient, both dynamically linked to the sliders. The scene should start with flash at 60%, ambient at 40%, exposure at 1.0s, and animation phase at 0.5. Include clear labels and a step counter showing total interactions performed.
